headline: Underarm roll-on, every morning
footnote: Day and week labels mark routine stages, not study timings. AI illustrations, not real results.
image_prompt: Empty background scene only: a pure white seamless paper backdrop, soft daylight from the upper left, a faint grey contact-shadow area on the right. Square 1080x1080. Keep the right 45% of the frame as an empty space, evenly lit, for a pack photo placed later, and keep the left half as a calm empty area for copy. No product, no bottle, no packaging, no text, no letters, no logos, no people, no faces, no skin, no hands.
photography_needed: Real, consented progress photos from a documented study of this product (same person, same light; the real pack in frame) to replace the AI frames before any use.
caption: Nonapeptide + AHA 6% Underarm Roll-On: Apply on clean and dry armpits using the roller and allow to dry before getting dressed; AM, every day. For external use only. Patch test recommended. The frames are AI illustrations of a routine, not study results.
adaptation_notes: Format #14 Progress / timeline (subtle remake): product in every frame, very small realistic change, labels are routine stages not timings, AI illustrations labelled; Severe by house rule.
writer: stand-in (Claude agent) following prompts/pipeline_brief_writer.md; user rules 2026-10-05 (active + strength shown, basis in footnote, no exaggeration, nothing pending)
frames_prompt: Three equal panels of the same Indian woman in her early 30s with medium-brown skin, an identical close crop of the raised arm from the shoulder to the elbow in a sleeveless top with the underarm area softly visible in every panel, same framing, angle and soft daylight from the upper left. Concern: a slightly darker underarm tone. Panel 1: the tone as it is; panels 2 and 3: the same area only very slightly lighter each time, none vanishing. The change is small and realistic, never dramatic. In every panel the lower-right corner (about 30% of the panel width and 40% of its height) is a plain, softly lit area that is intentionally empty, reserved for the real pack to be placed later.
